response.reason: Each numbered segment yields atomic contracts: initial entry (NL1), transition endpoints with events/guards captured in transition_groups plus separate action/effect/state_action contracts for explicitly stated behaviors (timer start/stop, cooking time display/update, cancel/update time). Self-loop retention (Cancel in DoorShut) is captured as state_retention. No termination state is explicitly stated in this NL (no explicit end/completion state), so no termination contracts are created. No cardinality or containment obligations are explicitly established since these are simple flat states without described composite/child hierarchy beyond the state machine itself. Guard disjointness is added where NL explicitly requires distinguishing alternatives (DoorOpenWithItem alternatives based on door closed with zero time vs cooking time entered).

decisions.strongest_defeater: The NL fully supplies state=Cooking, phase=entry, and action='start timer', which would let S4 certify the action as present if the exact carrier held any action content, but the completed S4 backend receipt returned verdict=false with a counterexample showing the exact entry-phase action is not attached, so this potential satisfying reading is excluded by the exact executed result.

decisions.reason: NL8 requires an exact stop-timer effect on the Door_Opened transition (transition:line:29, Cooking -> DoorOpenWithItem). The closed inspection_equivalent_facts show effects: [] on this exact carrier, and the raw pyfcstm text confirms only '/Door_Opened' with no effect statement, establishing the exact absence on the exactly bound locus. The alternative framing that this reflects a model-wide absence of any timer variable is a competent but non-defeating alternative characterization of the same underlying fact; it does not rebut that the exact bound transition carrier lacks the required effect, so it survives only as an undercutting reading.
decisions.strongest_defeater: Because no timer variable exists anywhere in the model (n_variables=0), the missing stop-timer effect on transition:line:29 could be characterized as an inherent, model-wide absence of timer state rather than an isolated defect specific to this one transition, though the exact bound carrier itself still shows no effect content.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem triggered by the door opening must carry an exact effect that stops the timer, per NL8 ('opening the door stops the timer').

The exact bound carrier has guard=null per the observed fact, and the S5 predicate (transition_guard_equals) was executed with terminal_state=unsupported/failure_kind=invalid_input, confirming no guard text exists to parse against the required value. branches.reason: This lens compared all 21 supplied NL contracts against the exact closed FCSTM transition inventory (16 transitions), exact source inventory, and transition-group alternatives. Every transition_endpoints contract (NL1-ENDPOINT-1, NL2-ENDPOINT-1, NL3-ENDPOINT-1/2, NL4-ENDPOINT-1/2, NL5-ENDPOINT-1/2, NL6-ENDPOINT-1/2, NL7-ENDPOINT-1, NL8-ENDPOINT-1/2/3) has an exact matching source->target edge with the correct triggering event in the closed FCSTM (transitions at lines 16-31), so these are satisfied and omitted. The initial_entry contract (NL1-INIT-1) is satisfied by transition:line:16 ([*] -> DoorShut). The state_retention contract (NL1-RETAIN-1) is satisfied by the DoorShut self-loop on Cancel (transition:line:17). The guard_disjointness contract (NL4-DISJOINT-1) is flagged because both alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem (to DoorShutWithItem on Door_Closed, to ReadytoCook on Cooking_Time_Entered) have distinct triggering events (Door_Closed vs Cooking_Time_Entered) in the closed model, which are structurally different events, not the same condition -- so this NL4-DISJOINT-1 requirement is actually satisfied at the event level; however the NL guard text mentions 'zero time set' as a qualifier on the Door_Closed alternative which has no guard field represented in the closed model (guard=null on transition:line:22), meaning the qualifier itself is dropped, a distinct effect/guard-fidelity concern already captured by other effect contracts but not exactly this disjointness contract, so it is omitted here as satisfied for the disjointness property specifically. The effect/action contracts (NL5-EFFECT-1, NL6-EFFECT-1, NL7-ACTION-1, NL8-EFFECT-1) are audited against the closed FCSTM's exact carrier transitions/states, all of which show empty effects/actions in the pyfcstm text and inspection-equivalent facts (all transitions have effects: [] and no state action/entry-exit blocks are present), so precise gaps are raised as candidates bound to the exact carrier refs.

branches.reason: This lens audited root reachability, event-consumer coverage, termination/dead-end behavior, and cross-wrapper continuation for the microwave FCSTM. All 6 declared states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability and verify_facts proved reachability for every state, so no reachability defect exists. All 8 declared events have non-empty reachable_consumer_state_refs/reachable_consumer_transition_refs equal to their declared sets, so event-consumer coverage is fully satisfied for every event; no coverage gap exists. Every leaf/operating state (DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking) has non-empty outgoing_transition_refs, so no deadlock/dead-end frontier fact exists to support a V1 candidate anywhere. There is no supplied termination_state role in any contract (no state_role marks a completion state), so the stable-termination audit does not apply. The one behavior-relevant finding under this lens's mandate is the guard-disjointness obligation NL-CONTRACT-NL4-DISJOINT-1: the closed FCSTM shows both DoorOpenWithItem alternatives (tr_0007 Door_Closed, tr_0008 Cooking_Time_Entered) as unguarded/distinct-triggered, so operationally they are already distinguishable by event alone; this is a satisfied contract and is omitted. No additional causal contracts (initial_entry/reachability/consumer-coverage gaps) are exposed by cross-view closure because the model closes cleanly on all these properties, so additional_contracts is empty and no candidates are emitted for this lens.
